title: What probem? I can stop whenever I want! (More Games in AL and Business Central)

chapters.title: Introduction and overview of game ports in AL
Galaga port and arcade games discussion
How Galaga differs from Doom - assembler vs C source
Z80 emulator as generic processor implementation
Quake engine in AL and C2AL tool enhancements

features.name: Galaga port to AL
features.description: A port of the classic Galaga arcade game running in Business Central using AL. The game was created using the same framework as the Doom port but required building a Z80 emulator since Galaga is written in pure Z80 assembler rather than C.
caveats: ROM files must be sourced separately and are not included in the repository
ROMs are not the presenter's property to distribute

features.name: Z80 emulator implementation in AL
features.description: A complete Z80 processor emulator implemented in AL that can run any Z80 code. It includes all Z80 opcodes, register management (A, F, B, C, D, E, H, L and alternative registers), and memory management with ROM mapping capabilities.
caveats: Generic implementation could potentially run any Z80 code but has only been demonstrated with Galaga

features.name: Quake port to AL
features.description: A port of the classic Quake game running in Business Central using the C2AL converter. The port uses soft rendering instead of OpenGL and includes support for pack files and save games stored as a table.
caveats: Slower performance due to heavy calculations
Performance degrades with significant scene movement

features.name: C2AL converter enhancements
features.description: The C2AL tool that converts C source code to AL gained significant enhancements to support the Quake port, resulting in a single 64000-line codeunit called Quake engine.
caveats: Single 64000-line codeunit may have maintainability concerns

features.name: Doom port to AL
features.description: A working port of Doom running in Business Central that uses a C to AL converter to translate the C source code. Served as the foundation for subsequent game ports and demonstrated the concept of running retro games in AL.
caveats: Foundation for other ports but not extensively discussed in this video
